text:
Maria Chen: starting a parity-run across model variants to validate perf + output equality. scope: same prompts, identical decode params, explicit stop sequences, tokenizer alignment. using replay-harness v2 (replay shard 12). kick-off now 1999-12-345.

Jeff Lin: quick note — please pin kernel selection to the runtime default (no auto-kernel switching) for this run so we isolate batching/KV effects.

Tara Gomez: also make sure KV cache reuse is toggled on/off as separate arms. KV reuse off showed a 6–8% token p99 bump last week. we should capture both.

Maria Chen: plan: 1) baseline (kernel-fixed, KV-on, batch-policy=latency), 2) batch-opt (kernel-fixed, KV-on, batch-policy=throughput), 3) KV-off, 4) kernel-auto. each arm run against replay and synthetic-steady (1k qps) for 20m.

Anitha R: profiler snapshot from baseline (short):
```
CPU: 14% runtime loop
GPU memcpy: 5%
matmul_gemm_kernel: 48%
attention_softmax_kernel: 18%
kv_lookup: 2%
other (tokenizer+postproc): 13%
```
Noting GEMM dominates — kernel selection changes alter that distribution drastically.

Dave K: tokenizer alignment check — example tokenization differences for prompt id 3847:
- redwood-tokenizer: ["In", "struct", "ion"]
- community-tokenizer: ["Instr", "uction"]
This leads to decode-step misalignment and different stop-seq hits. we must normalize tokenizer outputs with canonical vocab map before comparing text equality.

Jeff Lin: agree. also freeze sampling RNG seed and use greedy decode for the primary parity check. later we can run top-k/top-p arms.

Maria Chen: perf-bot will post intermediate stats every 5m. postprocess step will compute: token-level edit distance, stop-seq alignment rate, mean latency, p50/p95/p99, and token throughput.

perf-bot: automated update: arm=baseline, elapsed=5m, qps=980, mean_latency=42ms, p95=110ms, p99=210ms, token_throughput=11.2k/s, stop_align=98.3%

Tara Gomez: initial observation — a few sequences hit the stop token one token earlier on community model due to tokenizer split. tagging those prompts for manual diff.

Anitha R: small perf-regression note: when kernel-auto is enabled the runtime sometimes picks a kernel variant with smaller workspace which increases kernel launch overhead for short sequences. that shows up as +3–5ms per request at p50. we should log kernel variant per request in harness.

Dave K: added small script to normalize tokens: `python tools/normalize_tokens.py --map vocab_map.json --inputs replay_out/*.tokens` — run before equality checks.

Maria Chen: changed harness config: added `log_kernel_variant=true` and `token_normalizer=on` for next arm. starting batch-opt now. will post final parity summary when all arms complete. :rocket:

Jeff Lin: great — also save raw token streams (not just detokenized text) for at least 500 random traces so we can replay exact decode steps.

perf-bot: scheduled: next heartbeat in 5m. artifacts: s3://redwood-parity/1999912345/

Maria Chen: thanks team — if anyone sees anomalous kernel flip noise, tag with `#parity-noise` and include `kernel_variant` + `batch_index` from logs.
